_provenance.what: Monster break data served to the GL client as the `BJ6A0KTt` (MonsterPartsBreakMst) and `7KCkJd1E` (MonsterPartsExtStatusMst) rows for every served part whose `bV34YIJQ` row carries a non-zero `e56NZY42` (MonsterBreakID).
_provenance.primary_source: aEnigmatic's per-encounter datamine gists (`<mission>.jp.py`): a `# Break` block per monster -- `# Hit points <base> (+<delta> after first BREAK)`, `# Duration <n>`, a 16-row per-weapon `# Damage` table -- and a `# Broken Form` stats/resist block. Every entry names its gist id, file and line range. Found by the operator 2026-10-11; it closed the Heavenly Flames PRO gap the wiki had no section for.
_provenance.corroboration: The Fandom wiki boss guides agree EXACTLY for 6 of the 8 parts. For the two Ymir shells the wiki is wrong (no INT section -> ADV values substituted; ADV broken DEF 200 vs the gist 2,000). The gist's JP and GL files agree with each other on every field, so the gist wins.
_provenance.why_a_community_source: Those two tables were TRANSMITTED, never shipped, and no recoverable corpus has them: 0 of the 6 ext-status tokens across 231,518 JP-oracle rows + 590,632 GL mst_decoded rows; no break table among the 192 declared F_* names of either the JP/Memorial or the JP original (AndApp) engine, and no offline filler or synthesized default in either; MEMORIUM V5.8/FR/SP (143 .dat) none; the AndApp archive's own 179-table MST set omits the battle tables entirely; community repo and wire-token searches return zero.
labels: COMMUNITY-DERIVED (datamine gist, wiki-corroborated), not first-party. Never cite this as recovered wire data.

break_hp is CX5D2V1j (raw BP points). break_delta_after_first is encoded as zW97Bico=1 + 8HnQR9Wx=delta: MonsterUnit::getMaxBp (GL 0x1b6c6b0-0x1b6c6c8) applies type 1 as base+value and type 2 as base*value/100, ONLY once BattleUnit::getBreakNum() >= 1; the pool re-arms at break end. Type 2 with value 0 would zero the pool -- never emit that.
broken{atk,def,mag,spr} replace 9NBV1XCS / Pn5w9dfh / 84FJM3PD / T8xMDAZ4 in the break row; while MonsterUnit::isBreak() those are what the stat getters return (0x1b65fbc).

resists{} are the BROKEN FORM's values (the gist's `# Broken Form` block) and OVERRIDE the ones copied from the part row: for Intangir, Antenolla and the 2-Headed Dragon the broken form loses its elemental immunity (99% -> 0% / 49% / -50%), which is exactly what breaking is for. Tokens: hn42BL3Q element (9), D9Nb7jgd status (8), f67khsQZ / Q1qLbx93 damage cuts, Rcqa1Zt7 debuff (7); CSV = comma-separated ints in listed order, matching the parts-row convention.

RHe5r72C IS REQUIRED AND SENT: MonsterUnit::getWeakWeaponPointRelationship 0x1b6c734 parseLists ext-status +0x38 and indexes all 16 entries with no length check, so an absent field is CommonUtils::StrToInt on a null std::string -- the 2026-10-11 first fault (si_addr 0). The values are the gist per-weapon `# Damage` table in equip-category order 1..16 (Dagger..Fist). EwZ40mt3 (+0x50) has the identical unguarded 16-index in BattleLibraScene::setLayoutWeakWeapon 0x202b208 (an entry == 1 shows an icon) and is sent as a DERIVED 0/1 flag list at the row max -- unverified, cosmetic.
break_description is the 6uvHX2JG text key; only 2 of 8 parts have a source (aEnigmatic/ffbe-gl-strings MST_MONSTER_PARTS_BREAK_DESCRIPTION.json: Ymir 'DEF Reduced').
gaps: Part 407031105 (a Bahamut variant with its own non-zero MonsterBreakID, HP 2.1e9 / ATK 30,000 / DEF 99,000) is in a gist monster line but in no battle group we serve. If a future mission uses it, add an entry here or the deriver zeroes its id (break off, crash-safe).
6uvHX2JG for 6 of 8 parts: no source (only 30 rows exist in the GL strings table).
